title: AI characters that respond using live game state, not scripted dialogue
author: Western_Bug_5085
selftext:
Hi everyone,

Our team at Convai has been working on Dynamic Context for AI characters in 3D environments.

The idea is to let a game pass live state into the character’s AI context. In this virtual range example, the project provides values like shots fired, targets hit, accuracy, objectives, and player progress, so the character can answer questions based on what actually happened in the scene.

Combined with Actions, that same AI character can also navigate, interact with objects, trigger behaviors, and react inside the environment.

The goal is to move from dialogue-only AI characters toward context-aware gameplay, while the game project still controls the actual state and behavior.

Full Dynamic Context Tutorial for Unreal Engine:  
[https://youtu.be/zGIBCWSElXs](https://youtu.be/zGIBCWSElXs)

Full Dynamic Context Documentation for Unreal Engine:  
[https://docs.convai.com/api-docs/plugins-and-integrations/convai-unreal-engine-plugin/features/dynamic-context](https://docs.convai.com/api-docs/plugins-and-integrations/convai-unreal-engine-plugin/features/dynamic-context)

Get started:  
[https://convai.com](https://convai.com)

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

comments.author: WhopperitoJr
comments.body:
Always great to see what the folks at Convai are working on! One question I have is what the average cost for an hour of gameplay is using this system. Of course that probably depends on numerous variables, but a rough estimate for a certain scenario would be great! And how are project teams managing usage costs? I want to offer cloud inference for a game I am developing, and I’m wondering if capping usage is viable.

I am working on similar tools including an Unreal plugin called [Personica AI](https://swamprabbitlabs.com/personica/) which is more free local/BYOM-based. Always looking to collaborate with others working on these kinds of systems :)
